rationale: Jesus sends his questioners to "go and learn" a saying and then quotes it: "I desire mercy, not sacrifice" (40.9.13, BSB). In this app's BSB those five words are exactly the first clause of Hosea 6:6, "For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings" (28.6.6, BSB); Matthew drops the opening "For" and the whole second clause. The Greek of Matthew in the critical text the BSB follows (Eleos thelo kai ou thysian, per Bible Hub; the Byzantine text reads Eleon) matches the Septuagint wording of Hosea 6:6 printed at ellopos.net word for word in that clause, and both follow the Hebrew's "and not" (welo). The range starts at 6:4 because the same Hebrew noun, chesed, sits behind the BSB's "loyalty" there ("your loyalty is like a morning mist") and its "mercy" in 6:6, which an English reader cannot see. Explicit because Matthew's own introduction marks the words as a text to be learned and the wording matches; Matthew quotes the same clause again at 12:7, a recurrence noted here and not authored as its own row.
